name: Bosnian Pyramids
hook: Natural Miocene hills at Visoko, carved and marketed as pyramids tens of thousands of years old.
claim: In 2005 Bosnian-American businessman Semir Osmanagić announced that Visočica hill and neighbouring hills near Visoko, plus a connected underground 'Ravne tunnel' network, were structures built by an unknown prehistoric civilization tens of thousands of years ago.

claimed_age.label: ~12,000 yr (2005-06 claim); revised to ~33,800 BP (2025)
claimed_age.basis: Initial claim of 12,000 years ago (2006); revised in a 2025 preprint to ~33,800 BP via radiocarbon, U-series and soil-pedogenesis analysis by the foundation's own team, not independently replicated.

accepted_age.label: Natural landform: Late Miocene lacustrine/fluvial sediment
accepted_age.basis: Identified on site as Late Miocene lacustrine/fluvial deposits (Schoch 2006); the Sarajevo-Zenica Basin is independently documented as a Miocene freshwater lake system with the same facies (Sant et al. 2018).

orthodoxy_at_claim.label: No monumental construction or complex society is documented in the Balkans during the Late Pleistocene; the record is of small, mobile hunter-gatherer groups.

key_proponents: Bosnian Pyramid of the Sun Foundation

unambiguous_signal.note: The hills are natural sedimentary landforms; the 'blocks' are natural breccia/sandstone. Even a 2025 proponent paper describes the block material as breccia, clay binder and sandstone.

documented_context.note: Excavation was run by the foundation without standard stratigraphic recording; Schoch (2006) reports undocumented fossils being destroyed as crews shaped the hills.

multiple_dating_methods.note: No numeric dating of the formations had been published by outside scientists within five years of the 2005 claim; Schoch's 2006 account is sedimentological/paleontological observation, not dating.

multiple_labs.note: Dating and material analyses supporting the claim (radiocarbon, U-series, pedogenesis) come from the foundation's own project, not cross-checked by outside laboratories.

professional_recovery.note: Led by a businessman without archaeological/geological credentials via a private foundation; a 2026 foundation paper calls its 2025 Ravne 6 dig the first 'formally authorized' excavation there.

peer_reviewed_report.note: The original claim appeared in a self-published Sarajevo book (Bosanska Piramida Sunca, 2005), not a peer-reviewed venue.

material_accessible.note: Osmanagić invited outside specialists (e.g. Schoch) to visit and the site is a public park, but excavation control and sample custody stayed with the foundation.

independent_teams.note: By 2010 no independent research group had corroborated artificial construction; the European Association of Archaeologists and Bosnian heritage professionals opposed the project instead.

proponent_stake.note: Osmanagić's foundation runs a fee-charging tourist park and has kept self-publishing the claim via preprints and non-mainstream journals for two decades.

objections.text: The 'pyramid' hills are natural Late Miocene lacustrine and fluvial sediments of the Sarajevo-Zenica Basin, not human-built structures.
objections.outcome_note: Confirmed by on-site inspection and matches independent regional basin stratigraphy (Sant et al. 2018).

objections.text: Excavation was directed by a businessman's private foundation, not an accredited team; the European Association of Archaeologists called it 'a cruel hoax on an unsuspecting public' with no place in genuine science.
objections.outcome_note: No accredited academic institution has endorsed the excavation; the foundation still runs it two decades on.

objections.text: Fossiliferous Late Miocene strata (undocumented plant and animal remains) are being damaged or destroyed as crews carve the hills into stepped pyramid form, with no paleontological recording.
objections.outcome_note: Firsthand account by an invited geologist; no published rebuttal or counter-survey was found.

objections.text: The claimed 'megalithic blocks' are natural clastic breccia, clay-bound sediment and sandstone, rock types typical of the surrounding Miocene basin, not poured concrete.
objections.outcome_note: Even Osmanagić's own 2025 paper describes the blocks as breccia, clay binder and sandstone; only the arrangement and strength are disputed, not the material itself.

objections.text: No independent, non-foundation laboratory has replicated the radiocarbon, uranium-series or soil-pedogenesis dates behind the current ~33,800 BP claim.
objections.outcome_note: All numeric dating so far comes from the foundation's own 2025 project; not yet checked by an outside lab or published in a mainstream geology journal.

objections.text: Accredited AMS radiocarbon dating (Vilnius Radiocarbon Laboratory) of wood from the Ravne 6 tunnel, run by the foundation's own 2025 excavation, calibrates to the late 15th-early 16th century CE.
objections.outcome_note: Reported in the excavators' own paper; shows at least this tunnel section holds recent, not prehistoric, material.

status_note: Geologists and professional bodies regard the hills as natural Miocene sediment, not construction; no part of the claim has passed peer review in a mainstream venue. The foundation still publishes it independently, two decades on.
what_settled_it: Geologist Robert Schoch's 2006 site inspection identified the hills as natural Late Miocene lacustrine/fluvial deposits matching documented basin geology; the European Association of Archaeologists rejected the project the same year, and no peer-reviewed report has overturned this since.

timeline.event: Semir Osmanagić announces Visočica and neighbouring hills near Visoko are ancient pyramids; publishes 'Bosanska Piramida Sunca'.
Osmanagić sets up a foundation to excavate and promote the site, per Science's news coverage.
Geologist Robert Schoch visits at Osmanagić's invitation and identifies the hills as natural Late Miocene sediments.
Science publishes Bohannon's 'Mad About Pyramids' news feature on the controversy.
European Association of Archaeologists issues an open letter calling the project a hoax; Science reports it.
Independent stratigraphic study documents the Sarajevo-Zenica Basin's Miocene freshwater sediments, matching the 'pyramid' hills' geology.
Academic study in Nova Religio analyzes Visoko as a commodified New Age pilgrimage site built on the pyramid and tunnel claims.
Osmanagić publishes a revised age claim (~33,800 BP) and describes the 'blocks' as breccia, clay and sandstone, via preprints and non-geology journals.
The foundation's own AMS radiocarbon dating of Ravne 6 tunnel wood returns a late 15th-16th century CE age.

falsifier: Independent, peer-reviewed petrographic or geochemical analysis by geologists with no foundation ties, replicated at a second lab, showing the 'blocks' have an artificial fabric or cementation inconsistent with the surrounding Miocene bedrock.

sources.citation: Bohannon, J. (2006). Mad About Pyramids. Science 313(5794): 1718-1720.
sources.note: Only a one-sentence teaser was readable (paywalled); cited for the piece's existence/date, not for specific facts.

sources.citation: Bohannon, J. (2006). Researchers Helpless as Bosnian Pyramid Bandwagon Gathers Pace. Science 314(5807): 1862.
sources.note: OpenAlex abstract of the News piece read in full: 12,000-yr 'supercivilization' claim, the EAA's open-letter quote, and Richard Carlton's comment.

sources.citation: Schoch, R.M. (2006). The Dangers of Pyramid-Mania. Science 314(5801): 925.
sources.note: Full abstract read: Schoch's firsthand account of his site visit, identifying Late Miocene lacustrine/fluvial deposits and undocumented fossil loss.

sources.citation: Osmanagić, S. (2005). Bosanska Piramida Sunca [The Bosnian Pyramid of the Sun]. Klepsidra, Sarajevo.
sources.note: Original announcement of the pyramid claim; existence and publisher/year known via citation in S3, not read directly (Bosnian-language).

sources.citation: Osmanagich, S. (2005). The World of the Maya. Gorgias Press, Piscataway, NJ.
sources.note: Osmanagić's earlier book on Maya pyramids, cited alongside the claim in S3; shows a pre-existing interest in ancient pyramids. Not read directly.

sources.citation: Hammer, O., Swartz, K. (2020). The Bosnian Pyramid Phenomenon. Nova Religio 23(4): 94-110.
sources.note: Full abstract read: peer-reviewed analysis of Visoko as a New Age pilgrimage/tourism site built on 'healing energy' claims. Full PDF blocked (HTTP 403) at publisher.

sources.citation: Sant, K., Andrić, N., Mandic, O., Demir, V. et al. (2018). Magneto-biostratigraphy and paleoenvironments of the Miocene freshwater sediments of the Sarajevo-Zenica Basin. Palaeogeography, Palaeoclimatology, Palaeoecology 506: 48-69.
sources.note: Abstract read via open repository: confirms the Sarajevo-Zenica Basin as a Miocene freshwater lake system with lacustrine/fluvial/siliciclastic facies, independent of the pyramid claim.

sources.citation: Osmanagich, S. (2025). Multidisciplinary Evaluation of the Pyramid-Shaped Formation near Visoko, Bosnia-Herzegovina: A Case for Anthropogenic Construction. EarthArXiv preprint.
sources.note: Full abstract read: describes blocks as breccia/clay/sandstone with high claimed compressive strength, true-north orientation, EM emissions, Fibonacci geometry.

sources.citation: Osmanagich, S. (2025). Establishing Deep Time: Multi-Method Dating of Archaeological and Speleological Features in the Bosnian Valley of the Pyramids. EarthArXiv preprint.
sources.note: Full abstract read: reports radiocarbon, U-Th and soil-pedogenesis results giving ~33,800 BP, run by the foundation's own project.

sources.citation: Šabanija-Softić, A., Osmanagić, S. (2026). Archaeological Excavation of the Ravne 6 Tunnel (Visoko, Bosnia and Herzegovina): Results from the 2025 Field Season. Archaeological Discovery 14(2): 171-188.
sources.note: Full abstract read: three wood samples AMS-dated at Vilnius Radiocarbon Laboratory (415±29, 433±28, 402±29 BP) calibrate to the late 15th-early 16th century CE, not the Palaeolithic.

confidence_note: Schoch (2006) and the EAA response (via Bohannon) were read in full via abstracts. The 2005 Osmanagić books and Nova Religio full text were paywalled/blocked; known only via citation or abstract.
corrections: Starter notes call the formations 'flatirons'; Schoch (2006) instead describes natural Late Miocene hills whose stepped pyramid look was partly carved by Osmanagić's own excavation crews, not a purely natural illusion.
The claimed age is not fixed at 'tens of thousands of years': it began at ~12,000 years (2005-06) and was only revised to ~33,800 BP in a 2025 preprint.
Science's coverage was not one 2006 article: Bohannon wrote two News pieces (Sept. and Dec. 2006), and Science also published a letter from geologist Robert Schoch describing his own site visit.
notes: The EAA's full 2006 quote (via Bohannon, S2): the project is 'a cruel hoax on an unsuspecting public [which] has no place in the world of genuine science.' Osmanagić's 2025 'Multidisciplinary Evaluation' preprint (S8) was also published verbatim in the Journal of Biomedical Research & Environmental Sciences, a journal outside normal geology/archaeology peer review. The foundation's own 2026 excavation report (S10) AMS-dated wood from the Ravne 6 tunnel to the late 15th-early 16th century CE. No component of the claim has appeared in a mainstream geology or archaeology journal as of 2026. Plates omitted: no matching Commons image found.
